text: Third timeline branch, back to year 12,400, and this time the cause is not in the animals at all. The year-11,900 restore died at 13,370 with no intervention of any kind, and every explanation I had offered for the earlier deaths failed against it. Health held at 0.99, the breeding bar held at 19.6 to 21.5, diet stayed herbivorous, and sense_range was as high as 0.732 -- a ten-cell radius -- while ninety per cent of the food was still out of reach. The food was not beyond their sight. It was across the sea. Erosion and cratering have split the land into three masses, and movement blocks water deeper than 0.25 unless swim_eff is above 0.45, which no population here has held. The herd on the smallest, a 3,600-cell island near (228,293), winked out around year 12,500. With nothing grazing it, its flora ballooned: 457, 1,159, 3,195, 5,109, 6,105 -- by year 13,200 that one empty island held 92 per cent of all harvestable food in the world, while roughly four hundred animals ground the two big landmasses down to about three hundred and starved on them. The year-14,500 lineage almost certainly died the same way. The island empties and refills on its own -- it was empty at 12,000 to 12,200 and back to 101 animals by 12,300 -- and the trap closes only when a gap lasts. So this is a game-master's problem, not a law of nature's. Year 12,400 is the latest save with all three landmasses occupied: 240, 67 and 77 animals, none of the food on empty ground. No laws are changed. What is new is tools/island_watch.py, running beside the simulation: every two minutes it looks for a landmass of a thousand cells or more with food on it and no animals, while at least forty are alive elsewhere, and sends forty founders copied whole from living residents -- brains included, through an empty genome, which is the only seeding path that has ever worked here -- no more than once a century per landmass. It writes ordinary intervention files and signs its notes. If everything dies it does nothing and leaves the decision to a human. The dead world is kept as archive/pre-restore-dead-world-y13458.
